Name: Cable Equation (Continuous)
Biological_Source: Signal propagation along axon/dendrite (Rm=8300-19200 Ω·cm², Ra=163.9-224 Ω·cm)
PyTorch_Implementation:
# Continuous form (solved via discretization)
class CableEquation(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, Rm, Ra, Cm):
        self.Rm = Rm  # Ω·cm²
        self.Ra = Ra  # Ω·cm
        self.Cm = Cm  # µF/cm²
    def forward(self, V, dV_dt):
        # ∂²V/∂x² ≈ (V[i+1] - 2V[i] + V[i-1]) / dx²
        d2V_dx2 = (V[1:] - 2*V[:-1] + V[:-1]) / (self.dx**2)
        d2V_dt2 = (1/self.Cm) * ((1/self.Ra)*d2V_dx2 - V/self.Rm)
        return d2V_dt2
Drosophila_Circuit_Application: Voltage propagation along projection neuron axon/dendrite, signal attenuation with distance
Implementation_Notes: Foundation for compartmental model; discretize into 640-1152 segments

Name: Cable Equation (Discretized)
Equation: Cm × dV_i/dt = G_i(V_parent - V_i) + G_i(V_child - V_i) - V_i/Rm where G_i = π·d·a·(Ra)⁻¹
PyTorch_Implementation:
class CompartmentalNeuron(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_segments=640):
        self.n_seg = n_segments
        self.V = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(n_seg) * -60)  # mV
        self.G_axial = self._compute_axial_conductances()

    def forward(self, V_parent, V_child, I_syn, dt):
        dV_dt = torch.zeros(self.n_seg)
        for i in range(self.n_seg):
            axial_in = self.G_axial[i-1] * (V_parent[i] - self.V[i]) if i > 0 else 0
            axial_out = self.G_axial[i] * (self.V[i] - V_child[i]) if i < self.n_seg-1 else 0
            leak = self.V[i] / self.Rm
            dV_dt[i] = (axial_in - axial_out - leak + I_syn[i]) / self.Cm
        self.V += dV_dt * dt
        return self.V
Drosophila_Circuit_Application: Voltage integration across 640-1152 dendritic compartments in projection neuron
Implementation_Notes: Use CVODE solver; each compartment is separate state variable

Name: Voltage Attenuation
Equation: V_atten = (v + 60.0) / 60.0 (normalized) OR V(x) = V(0) × exp(-x/λ) where λ = √(Rm×d/(4×Ra))
PyTorch_Implementation:
class VoltageAttenuation(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, lambda_eletrotonic=150):  # µm
        self.lambda = lambda_eletrotonic

    def forward(self, V0, distance):
        # Exponential decay with distance
        V_atten = V0 * torch.exp(-distance / self.lambda)
        return V_atten
Drosophila_Circuit_Application: Signal loss across dendritic branches (46+ µm extent); determines effective integration distance
Implementation_Notes: Implement as distance-dependent gain; shorter distances have higher weights

Name: Electrotonic Length Constant
Biological_Source: Cable theory characterization (λ ≈ 100-200 µm for Drosophila PNs)
Equation:
λ = √(Rm × d / (4 × Ra))
L_electronic = L_anatomical / λ
For Drosophila: λ ≈ 150 µm, L_anat ≈ 46 µm → L_elec ≈ 0.3
PyTorch_Implementation:
def compute_electrotonic_length(Rm, Ra, diameter):
    lambda_const = torch.sqrt((Rm * diameter) / (4 * Ra))
    return lambda_const

def compute_segment_RC(Rm, Cm, diameter, length):
    R_segment = Rm / (3.14159 * diameter * length)
    C_segment = Cm * 3.14159 * diameter * length

Name: Axial Resistance (Compartmental Coupling)
Equation:
Ra_segment = Ra × L / (π × (d/2)²)
Ra_segment_ohms = Ra_segment × 1000

PyTorch_Implementation:
def compute_axial_resistance(Ra, length, diameter):
    Ra_seg = Ra * length / (3.14159 * (diameter/2)**2)
    return Ra_seg

def compute_coupling_conductance(Ra, length, diameter):
    Ra_seg = compute_axial_resistance(Ra, length, diameter)
    G_coupling = 1.0 / Ra_seg
    return G_coupling

Name: Cable Equation + ARCH-9 Enhancement
Biological_Source: Cable equation naturally separates fast (capacitive) and slow (resistive) components
Equation:
Fast: Cm × dV/dt (immediate response to input)
Slow: V/Rm (membrane leak, time constant τ_m = Rm × Cm)
Coupling: (1/Ra) × ∂²V/∂x²
PyTorch_Implementation:
class DualChannelCable(nn.Module):
    def forward(self, V_parent, V_child, I_syn, dt):
        # Fast capacitive component
        I_cap = self.Cm * dV_dt  # Immediate response
        # Slow resistive component
        I_res = V / self.Rm  # Exponential decay with tau_m
        # Coupling component
        I_axial = (1/self.Ra) * d2V_dx2
        # Combined
        dV_dt = (1/self.Cm) * (I_axial - I_res + I_syn)
        return dV_dt
Drosophila_Circuit_Application: Biophysically separates fast synaptic response (ms) from slow integration (10-50 ms)
Implementation_Notes: Natural decomposition emerges from cable equation physics
